title: Seazn capture descriptor, v1: GET /api/v1/capture/codes/{code}
description: The 200 answer to GET /api/v1/capture/codes/{code}?slot=&phone= (capture QR v2 spec 2026-10-01 §6.3.1, §6.4; amended §17.5, R5 final, agreed with capture 2026-10-01): a union on `state`. `waiting` is the waiting shape; warming, live, ending, completed and failed are the session shape. Each state admits only its own fields, and a field from another state is refused, never ignored. A field that is not required is omitted when it does not apply, never sent as null (§4). There is no hint field: a session shape without cred is the hint to claim (§6.3.1). $defs.refusal is the body of every refusal (§4). This route never sends 410 (ask 8). Vendored into the capture repo; its sha256, parity with its zod twin and its fixtures are pinned by apps/web/src/server/api-v1/__tests__/capture-contract.test.ts.

oneOf.description: No session for the slot, a session still requested or provisioning (then pollSeconds is 5), a session that ended before warming, or a caller without ?phone= (§6.3.1).

label.description: "{side A} v {side B}", or "Match {n}" in the competition's locale while a side is not yet known; at most 200 characters, cut with one "…" (§6.4, W25, §17.6).

venueTimezone.description: IANA zone: the division's override, then the org's timezone, then UTC (§6.4).

scheduledStart.description: fixtures.scheduled_at as epoch seconds; omitted, never null, when the fixture has none (§6.4, §4).

pollSeconds.description: How often the phone polls and beats, 5 to 300 seconds (§6.6, §6.9).

autoAllowed.description: Whether the server may start the broadcast on its own; always false in PR-1 (§6.4, §7.1).

destinationName.description: The pre-picked destination's label, at most 80 characters cut with one "…"; null when there is none or it is archived (§6.4, §6.7.3, §17.6).

overlayUrl.description: The scorebug overlay page, or null when the org lacks streaming.overlay (§6.4.1, W11, W18).

heartbeatUrl.description: Where the phone POSTs its beats: {origin}/api/v1/capture/codes/{code}/beats (§6.4, §6.3.2).

startUrl.description: Where the phone POSTs Go live: {origin}/api/v1/capture/codes/{code}/start (§6.4, §6.3.4).

stage.description: Where the match sits in its stage (W28, added 2026-10-06): the scheduler board's chip, the round's role, the pool and (2026-10-07) the label the phone shows. On the waiting shape and every session state; omitted, never null, when no code can be produced. Recomputed on every read.

code.description: Exactly the scheduler board's chip for this match, 1 to 8 characters: a bracket round's short code (QF, SF, F, 3rd, R16, WB2, LB3, GF, Q1, E, E2, …) or R{round} where the board codes no round (a league, a group, a Swiss round). In the language the label uses (the org's locale, W25): a Spanish org reads CF for a quarter-final.

role.description: The engine's round role for this match, serialised verbatim: kind, plus n or entrants where the role has one (W28).

kind.description: The role's kind. An OPEN string: today's values are `round_of`, `quarter_final`, `semi_final`, `final`, `winners_final`, `losers_round`, `losers_final`, `grand_final`, `grand_final_reset`, `third_place`, `qualifier1`, `eliminator`, `qualifier2`, `rung`, `plain_round`. Consumers show nothing for an unknown kind — a newer server may send one (W28).

n.description: The round number the role carries (losers_round, rung, plain_round), from 1 (W28).

entrants.description: round_of only: how many entrants the round starts with, from 2 (W28).

pool.description: The key of the match's pool, one capital letter (A, B, …), present only for a pooled group match. Never the pool's display name (W28).

label.description: What the phone shows for the stage, verbatim, 1 to 40 characters, in the org's locale (W28, added 2026-10-07): the pool's word and key, " · ", then the code ("Group A · R1", "Grupo A · R1") for a pooled match, else exactly the code. Omitted, never cut, when it would not fit; show nothing then.

oneOf.description: An open session warming up; cred only to the slot's current phone (§6.3.1, §5.3).

preferred.description: The transport to publish on. It never names a null shape: "rtmps" whenever cred.srt is null (§6.4, A18).

playbackUrl.description: The bare HLS manifest, with no query (§6.4, W14).

holdWindowSeconds.description: Per transport, how long the ingest holds a dropped publish before the broadcast ends; each at most 999 (§6.4).

scoreUpdates.description: "realtime" when overlayUrl carries a key, "polled" otherwise (§6.4).

refusal.description: Every refusal: `code` is the machine word the phone keys its copy on; `message` is a developer string, never shown (§4). This route answers 401 code_ended for an unknown code, a wrong tok or an ended code, and 404 not_a_stream_code for a malformed code; 422, 429 (with Retry-After) and 503 count as no evidence (§6.3.1, §10.1).

code.description: The machine word the phone keys its copy on (§4).

message.description: A plain English developer string; the phone never shows it (§4).

sid.description: already_live only: the session that is already live (§6.3.4, ask 4).

startedBy.description: already_live only: who started it (§6.3.4, ask 4).

code.description: The machine word the phone keys its copy on (§4).

message.description: A plain English developer string; the phone never shows it (§4).
